sourceAsset.surfaceAndRig: MPFB core adult surface, default skeleton and weights, CC0-1.0
sourceAsset.sourceGenderDisclosure: The frozen source asset was built with a male macro. Current female appearance is a project-authored visual adaptation of this source topology, not an independently generated female macro or a scan.

modifications: Independent per-role geometry clones preserve original skin indices and weights.
Female jaw/cheek/nose/brow surface refinements, lightly adjusted practical clothing surface.
Original fitted scalp, low ponytail and tapered framing locks for patient; short side sweep for therapist.
Original oval eyes, upper eyelids, brows and restrained eye highlights replace source sphere details.
Role-specific skin vertex colours and clothing materials.
No lower-leg vertices below0.60m changed; no skeleton bones changed.

futureReplacement.requiredMedia: Licensed rigged 3D mesh with proper deformation weights; a talking-avatar video alone cannot replace the interactive avatar.
requiredRuntimeContract: root Y-up metres and local+Z forward; separate skeleton per actor
bone map for root, head, jaw, upperleg01.L/R, lowerleg01.L/R, foot.L/R, upperarm01.L/R, lowerarm01.L/R and wrist.L/R, or an explicit adapter
actor methods setPose, setPosition, face, setLocomotion, setGaitPhase, setTalking, setFootwear, stop, update and getBodyReferencePosition
role-aware footwear and clothing states, suitable seated/exam/gait poses
professor review of contact, limb reach and pedagogical labels after replacement
checks: Record source licence and author attribution.
Check separate skeletons, finite geometry and stable ankle targets.
Inspect close frontal/side face, seated view, standing view and face motion.
Inspect shoe-floor alignment, chair contact, hair/clothing collisions and examination visibility.
Do not reuse source-specific surface refinement on a different topology without adapting it.

limits: First visual refinement of a fictional teaching character; not photorealistic.
No actual person identity or exact likeness.
No new patient scan, gait calibration or clinical validity.
Appearance is subjective and should be reviewed separately from clinical teaching accuracy.
